answer: Sybils fail once identity must be bonded: each agent escrows a time-locked, appraised bond - the economy's jade, rare and costly to mint - before trading. A single operator can no longer harbor a swarm of personas, since every fake needs its own escrow, and any duplicate takes a sable mark on the shared ledger, forfeiting principal. Attacker cost then scales linearly with identity count, not near-zero.
